target_customer: Health-conscious US consumers who pay out of pocket for an at-home urine test of chemical exposures (BPA, phthalates and later others)
problem: People cannot see which everyday chemicals such as plastics additives are in their bodies, so they cannot act on exposure.
business_model: DTC test kit and program, roughly $399 test to $999 program per a directory listing, plus NIH SBIR grants

founders.name: Jenna Hua
founders.background_notes: Registered dietitian and environmental health scientist per the company about page. YC page lists one founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed lab partnerships, validated urine assays for chemical biomarkers and a consumer reporting layer. Hard parts were lab and clinical validity rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Lab testing is outsourceable and kits are copyable, though grant-funded research and survey data give a modest edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it. Company remains active per YC.

market_need_then: Growing consumer interest in endocrine disrupting chemicals and plastics exposure, and the 23andMe style direct to consumer testing model was familiar by 2019. No hard spend data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Educational and approachable, tagline Real science for real life

branding.community_and_virality: Social accounts exist on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Pinterest and X, no press about the brand found

brand_strength.rationale: Little independent evidence of brand pull. Name echoes a health marker idea, but no source describes it.

outcome_analysis: Million Marker remains active with a two person team per YC. It appears to be funded mainly by non dilutive NIH SBIR grants and a small crowdfunding round rather than venture rounds, so it has stalled at small scale rather than failed. The scientist founder fits the problem, but there is no public evidence of venture scale traction, and the consumer testing price point may limit growth.
notes: Unverified funding from single snippets or aggregators: NIH R43 about $218,790 (2022) and R44 about $1,028,322 (2023) from api.ai-analytics.org; a directory claims nine NIH awards totaling $4.78M FY2022 to 2026; Employbl lists $150K YC pre-seed and $286K equity crowdfunding. None recorded as rounds. Competition near 2019 not found in dated sources; one UK alternative (lastinghealth) surfaced without a date, so list left empty. Second YC founder or team member not identified.
